bottlenecks.reading: The scarce, capital-heavy input of the whole competitive set is AI compute and data-center capacity, and each rival adds it with its own balance sheet. META guides 2026 capital expenditures (including finance-lease principal) to 135-145 billion USD (narrowed from 130-145), spent 34.9 billion in Q3 2026 against operating cash flow of 32.8 billion (free cash flow negative 2.1 billion), and says it is still developing 2027 capacity plans. Alphabet's last-twelve-month capex is 132.4 billion with Q2 2026 free cash flow negative 5.9 billion; Amazon's purchases of property and equipment are 173.0 billion over twelve months (free cash flow negative 7.6 billion). How long compute stays scarce is not evidenced by an industry source in this lane; what the filings show is that funding it already exceeds operating cash flow at META, Alphabet and Amazon.

META's growth in the latest quarter comes from yield per ad impression, not from users: in Q3 2026 ad impressions rose 10% and the average price per ad 14% while family daily active people rose only 3% (3.64 billion). The scarce thing META sells is measurable, AI-ranked attention in saturated markets; management attributes the gain to AI-driven engagement, recommendations and monetization (a management statement, not independently measured). Like-for-like rivals are user-constrained too: Snap North America DAU fell 7% and Pinterest U.S. and Canada MAU grew 4% in Q2 2026, so the ad-dollar gains of Snap (+19%) and Pinterest (+18%) also rest on pricing and ARPU.

Distribution and ad signals are controlled by two competitors: Apple (iOS data-use changes and Safari limit ad targeting and measurement while Apple expands its own advertising business) and Google (Android integration of competing products, Chrome cookie policy). The 10-K treats this as structural and ongoing, and the dependency has no capacity-addition date: it can only be hedged by owning more first-party signal and engagement.

Paid adoption of META's next-platform hardware is not yet visible in its own numbers: Reality Labs revenue was 1.276 billion USD in the first nine months of 2026 against 1.252 billion a year earlier (Q3 2026: 443 million against 470 million) with a Q3 operating loss of 4.129 billion; management expects 2026 Reality Labs losses of 18-19 billion USD and around 15 billion in 2027 as investment is reallocated to AI. Apple's wearables, home and accessories line alone was 7.9 billion USD in its June 2026 quarter (+6.5%).

Competitors monetize frontier AI through paid consumption, META through advertising yield: Google Cloud revenue grew 82% to 24.8 billion USD in Q2 2026 and AWS grew 37% (Amazon also booked 53.4 billion of other income mainly from its Anthropic investments), while META reports no AI-model or cloud revenue line (Family of Apps other revenue, which holds WhatsApp paid messaging and subscriptions, was 1.1 billion USD in Q3 2026). META launched its first frontier model (Muse and Muse Wonder) in Q3 2026 per management; whether it produces paid adoption outside ads is not evidenced yet.

bottleneck_potential.reading: META is a bottleneck on one thing it already owns: AI-ranked attention of 3.64 billion daily people, sold as measurable ad yield (ARPP 17.72 USD in Q3 2026 against 14.46 a year earlier, +23%). It is not a bottleneck on compute: it is a buyer of it, guiding 2026 capex of 135-145 billion USD with Q3 free cash flow of -2.12 billion, 454.5 billion of non-cancelable commitments and 355.7 billion of leases not yet commenced; Alphabet and Amazon add the same capacity on their own balance sheets (Alphabet Q3 free cash flow -9.1 billion, Amazon TTM -42.4 billion) and Amazon lists new AWS agreements with Meta. How long the attention position lasts depends on platform gatekeepers it does not control (Apple iOS/Safari data rules, Google Android/Chrome), which the 10-K treats as structural.

share_trajectory.reading: META is taking share from every named advertising competitor on same-quarter numbers: Q3 2026 advertising +25.9% (63.06 vs 50.08 billion USD) against Google advertising +10.6% (82.01 vs 74.18; YouTube ads +9.2%), Amazon advertising services +10.9% (19.64 vs 17.70, partly Prime Day timing) and Pinterest revenue +12%. META advertising as a share of Google advertising rose from 67.5% in Q3 2025 to 76.9% in Q3 2026 (61.9% Q1 2025, 71.2% Q1 2026), and META took about 57% of the 22.9 billion USD added by these four sellers in the year. Engagement share against TikTok and YouTube cannot be measured (TikTok private, YouTube usage undisclosed); the 10-K says TikTok has reduced some users' engagement. In hardware META is flat (Reality Labs 9M 2026 revenue 1.276 billion against 1.252) while Apple's wearables line is about 7.9 billion a quarter.

competitive_position.reading: Stronger than Google and Amazon in advertising growth (26% against about 11% each in Q3 2026) and far stronger than Snap and Pinterest in scale and profitability (Snap Q2 2026 operating margin negative, DAU 493 million with North America -7%; Pinterest Q3 revenue +12% and decelerating, US and Canada MAU +4%); META's FY2025 operating margin was 41.4% against Alphabet's 32.0%. Weaker than Google and Amazon in paid AI monetization outside ads: Google Cloud grew 103% to 30.7 billion USD in Q3 2026 with 11.1 billion operating income and AWS 39% to 46.0 billion, while META reports no cloud or model revenue line (Family of Apps other revenue, which holds WhatsApp paid messaging and subscriptions, was 1.1 billion, +59%). Weaker than Apple in consumer hardware and dependent on Apple and Google for distribution and ad signals.

threats.reading: Regulation and litigation are the evidenced threats: the August 2026 agreement with 52 attorneys general costs up to about 18.59 billion USD (9.89 billion charged in Q3 2026, about 5.3 billion contingent and unaccrued) plus under-18 product changes in the US, which the 10-Q warns can cause disproportionate engagement losses if YouTube and TikTok do not adopt the same measures; the EU DMA 'subscription for no ads' decision may force changes with 'a significant impact to our European business and revenue' (Europe 21.7% of Q3 revenue); the FTC appeal seeks Instagram and WhatsApp divestiture; the EU imposed free WhatsApp Business API access for AI providers in June 2026. Substitution: TikTok (named) for user time, and AI assistants of Google and others for discovery (hypothesis, no META figure). China: meaningful revenue from China-based resellers can be cut by governments (share undisclosed) and China already ordered the Manus unwind. Funding: about 37.5 billion USD of equity raised in October 2026 and a planned 60 billion ATM dilute holders if capex does not pay back.

bear.event_he: צמיחת מספר הצפיות במודעות, שירדה מ-19% ל-10% בשלושה רבעונים, נעצרת כמעט לגמרי, והעלאות המחיר למודעה לא מספיקות כדי להחזיק צמיחה של 20%.
ההוצאה להשקעות (135-145 מיליארד דולר ב-2026, תזרים חופשי שלילי ברבעון השלישי) ממשיכה לעלות ב-2027 בלי הכנסות חדשות מבינה מלאכותית, והתשואה על ההון החדש נשארת נמוכה (כ-15%).
בעלי המניות ממשיכים לממן: מעבר להנפקה של כ-37.5 מיליארד דולר באוקטובר 2026, החברה מפעילה את תוכנית מכירת המניות לשוק (כ-60 מיליארד דולר) דרך מניות Class C החדשות.
תביעות הנוער מתרחבות: הסכום המותנה של 5.3 מיליארד בהסכם התובעים הכלליים משולם, ומשפטי מחוזות בתי הספר מפברואר 2027 מוסיפים חיובים, כמו החיובים של 2.4 ו-9.89 מיליארד ב-2026.
באירופה (כ-22% מההכנסות ברבעון השלישי) הרגולטור מחייב מודעות פחות מותאמות אישית, והחברה עצמה כותבת שזה עלול לפגוע משמעותית בהכנסות האירופיות.

base.event_he: הרבעון הרביעי של 2026 מגיע לפחות לאמצע התחזית (74.5 מיליארד דולר, צמיחה של כ-24%), כמו ב-7 מתוך 7 הרבעונים האחרונים שבהם החברה עקפה את התחזית.
ב-2027 ההכנסות צומחות בכ-20%: מודלי הדירוג והפרסום ממשיכים להעלות את המחיר למודעה ואת ההמרות, ומודעות שותפות (קצב של מעל 15 מיליארד בשנה) ממשיכות לגדול.
ההפסד של Reality Labs מצטמצם לכ-15 מיליארד דולר ב-2027 (מ-18-19 מיליארד ב-2026), והרווחיות התפעולית עולה חלקית.

עסקת המכירה העתידית של 40 מיליון מניות (כ-24.9 מיליארד דולר, עד נובמבר 2027) היא אירוע חוזי שאינו בחישוב: גרסת המנוע לא יודעת לסמן הון חוזי כמחויב, ולכן לא המזומן ולא המניות נכנסו (ההשמטה מגדילה את הערך הבסיסי בכ-4 דולר למניה). המניה המועדפת (12.5 מיליארד) מחושבת כהתחייבות קודמת למניות, בקיזוז 12.46 מיליארד הכסף שהתקבל, ולא כ-17-20 מיליון מניות חדשות.

bull.event_he: העוזר האישי Muse (מעל 10 מיליון משתמשים בארה"ב וקנדה בשישה שבועות, כרבע משתמשים בו מדי יום) מושק גלובלית ומתחיל להכניס כסף ב-2027 מעמלות קנייה ומנויים, כפי שההנהלה אומרת שאפשרי.
עלות ההפעלה של מודלי הבינה המלאכותית יורדת פי 10 ויותר בשנה הקרובה כפי שהמנכ"ל צופה, כך שההשקעות מתחילות להחזיר רווח והרווחיות חוזרת לכ-42% כמו ב-2024.
הכנסות אחרות (הודעות בתשלום בוואטסאפ ומנויים, מעל 15 מיליון מנויי Meta One) ממשיכות לצמוח בקצב של כ-59% בשנה ומוסיפות מקור הכנסה שאינו פרסום.
לא נדרשת תוכנית מכירת המניות לשוק של כ-60 מיליארד, כי התזרים מכסה את ההשקעות.

growth_anchor.reason: No FY2027 guidance exists (outlook only at the Q4 call), so growth rests on META's own trajectory: Q3 2026 +26% and the Q4 guide 73-76B (+22% to +27%, a conservative guider that beat 7 of 7 quarters), with management saying it will sustain strong revenue growth through 2027. Base 20%: a step down from about 27% in 2026 because impressions growth has decelerated from +19% to +10% in three quarters and the price-per-ad gains (+14%) must carry more; it sits just below the attributed FY2027 consensus (311.5B, about +21%, a cross-check, not evidence). Bull 26%: the 2026 pace holds because new AI revenue (Muse commerce fees and subscriptions, business messaging, partnership ads over a 15B run rate growing +97%) adds on top of ranking gains, as management says can begin in 2027. Bear 13%: impressions stall near zero and pricing gains halve, plus a macro ad slowdown and EU less-personalized ads (Europe 22% of Q3 revenue) - between the 2023 rebound (+16%) and a 2022-style stall.

mature_margin.reason: Operating margin after SBC (SBC is inside META's GAAP costs). Own history: 24.8% (2022 trough), 34.7% (2023), 42.2% (2024 peak), 41.4% (2025); FY2026 implied about 31% reported and about 35% ex the 9.89B AG charge (expense guide 175-179B on about 256B revenue). Base 37%: partial recovery as the Reality Labs loss narrows to about 15B in 2027 (about +1.5 points) and capex growth slows, but depreciation of a 250B+ asset base and AI token costs keep it below the 2024-25 level. Bull 42%: back to the 2024 peak as AI products monetize the installed compute. Bear 30%: depreciation, cloud capacity and recurring legal costs keep expense growth above revenue (Q3 2026 ex-charge 35%, FoA margin down 22 points y/y). Repair: bear 29% at maturity (was 30%) to match the bear cash-cost path (the explicit years go to 26% in 2029, toward the 2022 trough); the yearly margin path is now set by cash_cost_ratio, starting ex the 12.29B legal charges.

sales_to_capital.reason: Incremental revenue per dollar of invested capital (equity + debt - cash and securities), from META's own balance sheets: 2021-2024 invested capital +57B for revenue +47B (about 0.82); end-2024 to Q3 2026 invested capital +140B for TTM revenue +77B (about 0.55) during the AI capex ramp (2026 capex guide 135-145B). Base 0.70: between the two as capex growth slows and the new capacity is absorbed; bull 0.85: the 2021-2024 efficiency returns; bear 0.55: the current ramp ratio persists (AI spend keeps rising faster than revenue).

tax_rate.reason: The Q4 2026 guide is 15-17% (midpoint 16%); Q3 2026 was 17% ex the nondeductible part of the legal charge. Reported rates are distorted by discrete items (87% Q3 2025, 2% 9M 2026), so the guided normal rate is used in every scenario; tax volatility (20.8B unrecognized tax benefits) is a risk, not a scenario lever.

growth_capex_pct.reason: Repair (review critical): the engine's reinvestment rule cut FY2027 capex to 84-104B, 25-40% below the FY2026 guide of 135-145B, with no evidence. Growth capex is set per period (share of revenue, maintenance capex stays at the engine's 9.26%) so TOTAL capex is: stub Nov-Dec 2026 about 36B in every scenario (FY2026 guide midpoint 140B less 9M 85.82B = about 54B for Q4, two thirds of it); FY2027 bear 145B, base 145B, bull 160B; FY2028 bear 140B, base 145B, bull 165B; FY2029 bear 120B, base 135B, bull 160B; FY2030 a step toward the engine's path (bear 14%, base 15.7%, bull 16.7% growth capex); from 2031 the engine's own rule. Basis: non-cancelable commitments due in 2027 are 121.41B against 45.85B due in the rest of 2026, when Q4 2026 capex is about 54B (ratio about 1.18), so committed 2027 spending alone points to about 140-145B; there is no FY2027 capex guide (given at the Q4 call), so the 2027-2029 path beyond the commitments is an analyst reading of that schedule. Bear keeps capex at or above the 2026 level while revenue slows (the bear event: spending keeps rising without new AI revenue); bull spends more to serve AI demand.

cash_cost_ratio.reason: Repair (review): the engine started the margin from the TTM GAAP operating margin 32.9%, which includes the 9.89B Q3 2026 attorneys-general charge and the 2.4B Q2 2026 legal charges; the same accruals sit in the 19.881B litigation claim, so they were counted twice. Cash cost ratios are set so that the operating margin after SBC and D&A (1 - cash costs - SBC - D&A, with the engine's SBC and D&A ratios) starts from the ex-legal level (TTM 37.9% ex the 12.29B; Q3 2026 ex-charge about 35%): base stub 38% (Q4 seasonally strongest), FY2027 36% (includes about 0.5 point of recurring legal costs; Reality Labs loss narrowing to about 15B), rising to 37% by 2030 (the evidenced mature_margin); bull 38%, 37%, then up to 42% (2024 peak) by 2031. Bear mechanisms sized: stub 37%, FY2027 31%, FY2028 27%, FY2029 26% (toward the 2022 trough 24.8%), then 27-28% and 29% from 2032: depreciation of 140B+ a year of capex (D&A about 9.3% of revenue in the engine against a build that would lift it toward 14-16% of bear revenue by 2028, about -5 to -6 points), recurring legal costs at the 2026 pace (2.4B + 9.89B charges, 5.3B contingent AG amount, youth trials; about -1 point) and less-personalized ads in the EU (Europe 22% of Q3 revenue). The D&A ramp is carried inside the cash cost ratio (the margin after D&A is what is set), not as a separate depreciation path: a visible simplification.

bear.reason_he: ההשקעות קפצו מ-37 מיליארד ב-2024 ל-70 מיליארד ב-2025 ולכ-140 מיליארד ב-2026, והחברה מגייסת הון במניות כדי לממן אותן; התשואה על ההון הנוסף בשלוש השנים האחרונות כבר ירדה לכ-15%. אם המרכזים החדשים לא יגדילו את ההכנסות מפרסום מספיק, התשואה תרד לכ-10%, קרוב לעלות ההון, ואז צמיחה כמעט לא מוסיפה ערך והמכפיל נמוך.

base.reason_he: לאורך 2020-2025 החברה הרוויחה כ-31% בממוצע על ההון שהשקיעה (כולל מוניטין), ובשנה האחרונה כ-29%; על ההון הנוסף של שלוש השנים האחרונות כ-15%, שעדיין לא כולל את כל ההכנסות מההשקעות האחרונות. ההכנסות ברבעון השלישי של 2026 צמחו בכ-26% והחברה עקפה את התחזית שלה בכל שבעת הרבעונים האחרונים, ולכן 20% (בין התשואה על ההון הנוסף לממוצע ההיסטורי) הוא המסלול הסביר ביותר: מעל עלות ההון, אבל לא השיא.

bull.reason_he: אם מודלי הבינה המלאכותית ממשיכים לשפר את מיקוד הפרסומות ואת זמן השימוש, ההכנסות גדלות מהר מספיק כדי שגם ההשקעה הענקית תחזיר כמו בעבר, כ-30% בשנה (הממוצע של 2020-2025 היה כ-31%); זו התשואה שהחברה כבר הוכיחה, לא שיא חד-פעמי, ולכן מכפיל גבוה מוצדק. עם זאת, התשואה על ההון הנוסף בשלוש השנים האחרונות היא כ-15% בלבד, ולכן 30% על ההשקעה החדשה עדיין לא הוכח בנתונים: זה תנאי של התרחיש השורי, לא עובדה.

key_risk.reading_he: ההשקעה בבינה מלאכותית גדולה מהתזרים: 135-145 מיליארד דולר ב-2026, תזרים חופשי שלילי ברבעון השלישי, התחייבויות של 454 מיליארד שאי אפשר לבטל, והחברה כבר מגייסת כסף מבעלי המניות (כ-37.5 מיליארד באוקטובר ותוכנית של עוד כ-60 מיליארד). אם ההכנסות החדשות מבינה מלאכותית יתעכבו, הרווחיות תישאר נמוכה והמניות ימשיכו להתדלל.

moat.note: Moat source evidenced: network scale (3.64 billion daily people) plus AI ranking that turns it into ad yield; META grew advertising 26% against Google about 11% and Amazon about 11% in Q3 2026. ROIC 28.7% last, 31.4% average (auto.json forensic), well above the 8% reference; incremental ROIC fell to 14.9% as capex rises, so the excess return is fading toward the cost of capital at the margin.

pricing_power.note: Price per ad +6%, +12%, +12%, +14% in the last four quarters while impressions also grew (+18% to +10%); ARPP +23% y/y. Prices are auction-set, so this is advertiser demand for META's conversion results, not list-price increases.

switching_costs.note: Advertisers have no long-term commitments and can cut spend quickly (Item 1A); users can substitute (TikTok named). What holds both is network size and conversion performance, not contractual lock-in.

retention.note: Family DAP rose from 3.54 to 3.64 billion in a year (+3%) with a small Q1 2026 dip (Iran disruptions, Russia WhatsApp restriction); the 10-K says TikTok reduced some users' engagement and younger users substitute other products. Advertiser retention is not disclosed.

customer_concentration.note: No customer at 10% or more of revenue in 2023-2025, millions of advertisers. One undisclosed cluster: China-based resellers generate 'meaningful revenue' (inside Asia-Pacific, 26.3% of Q3 revenue); its size is a gap.

market_size.note: META already holds about 27% of worldwide digital ad spend (EMarketer, attributed forecast) and reaches most internet users; further growth must come from yield, new surfaces (WhatsApp, Threads, partnership ads 15 billion run rate) and new AI products, not from new users.

competition.note: META took about 57% of the incremental ad dollars among META, Google, Amazon and Pinterest in Q3 2026 and its advertising rose from 67.5% to 76.9% of Google's; Snap and Pinterest are sub-scale. TikTok is unmeasured (private).

substitutes.note: Short video (TikTok, YouTube) is a named substitute for user time; AI assistants as a substitute for feed-based discovery and ads are a hypothesis with no META figure. Current ad growth shows no substitution in the numbers yet.

management.note: Revenue delivery is excellent: 7 of 7 quarters above the guided midpoint (mean ratio 1.041, auto.json track_record); costs cut (headcount -15% y/y). Against that, the capex guide rose from 115-135 to 135-145 billion USD during 2026 and Reality Labs loses 18-19 billion a year on about 2.2 billion of flat revenue, with profitability undated.

capital_allocation.note: Through 2025 buybacks beat SBC (diluted shares 2,888 million in 2020 to 2,574 million in 2025; FY2025 buybacks 26.2 billion USD against SBC 20.4 billion). In 2026 the direction reversed: no buybacks in 9M 2026, Q3 free cash flow -2.12 billion, about 37.5 billion of equity raised in October (25.0 billion forward at 625 USD, 12.5 billion 6.50% mandatory convertible preferred) plus a planned 60 billion ATM. Incremental ROIC 14.9% is still above the cost of capital, but falling; the payback of the AI capex is unproven.

governance.note: Controlled company: Class B (ten votes) gives the CEO majority voting control; new non-voting Class C (effective 2027-01-19) is expected to be used for equity offerings, compensation and acquisitions, widening the dilution channel without diluting control (Founder Alignment Agreement of 2026-10-20).

regulation.note: Recurring legal costs (2.4 billion USD Q2, 9.89 billion Q3 2026; non-current legal accruals 8.3 billion), youth trials continuing in 2027, EU DMA/DSA and WhatsApp API actions against 21.7% European revenue, FTC divestiture appeal pending, AI copyright trials from May 2027.

technology_ai.note: AI in the core ads business is evidenced in META's own numbers (price per ad +14%, ARPP +23%, ad growth well above Google's). AI outside ads (Muse, Muse Wonder, 10 million setups per management, subscriptions, API) has no paid revenue yet, while Google Cloud already earns 30.7 billion a quarter on AI: that part is a hypothesis and moves no number.

geopolitics.note: Revenue is global (Asia-Pacific 26.3%, Europe 21.7% of Q3 2026) with an undisclosed China-reseller share that governments can cut; China ordered the Manus unwind (completed August 2026). Assets are 88% in the US; chip and server supply countries are not disclosed.

cyclical.reason: Revenue grew in five of six years 2020-2025; the only decline (2022, -1.1%) came from iOS signal loss plus an ad recession and was followed by +16%, +22%, +22% and about +27% in 2026. Advertising has macro beta (sized in the bear) but no commodity-style cycle to normalize.

debt_like_claims.reason: 6.50% Series A mandatory convertible preferred (12.5M preferred shares), issued 2026-10-29 after the Q3 balance sheet, liquidation preference 12.5B, converts about 2029-08-15 into 17.0-20.0M Class A shares. Repair (review): the 12.458B net proceeds (dc_eq_pref_net_oct2026, 8-K dc_8k_20261029) were received after the 2026-09-30 balance the engine opens from, and this engine version's pack has no input for a post-balance-sheet cash event (capital_events is not a pack option), so the claim is carried NET of its cash: 12.5B liquidation preference - 12.458375B net proceeds = 41.625M. Claim and cash enter together (net), never the claim alone. The 6.5% dividend (about 812.5M a year) above the yield on the cash is not separately charged (small, conservative to omit is not claimed); conversion shares are not also counted.

Legal-related accruals at 2026-09-30 (11.577B current + 8.304B non-current, 10-Q), led by the August 2026 attorneys-general agreement (payments up to 18.59B, about 12.7B in annual installments over 10 years). These were charged to earnings already, so the forecast cash flows never pay them; they are a cash claim ahead of the shares that the debt lines miss. The 5.3B contingent AG amount not accrued and the pending youth trials are not added (contingent: bear and key risk).
